reason: The text names Shiphrah (שִׁפְרָה) and Puah (פּוּעָה) as Hebrew midwives (מְיַלְּדֹת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּת), who are ordinary working women. Unlike the patriarchs (Jacob and his sons) or royal figures (Pharaoh and his daughter), these named individuals are depicted as regular professionals performing everyday duties. Despite Pharaoh's command, they represent ordinary people engaged in normal work, making them clear examples of named characters who are regular people rather than legendary or royal figures.
